english.title: Remove a drug of a temporary class from the place of importation with intent to evade prohibition
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[removed]_
(B)_[assisted in the removal of]_
(C)_[were concerned in the removal of]_

drugs subject to a temporary class drug order, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DRUGS..), the importation of which was

(D)_[prohibited]_
(E)_[restricted]_

by virtue of section 3 of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, from

(F)_[their place of importation]_
(G)_[an approved wharf]_
(H)_[an examination station]_
(I)_[a transit shed]_
(J)_[a customs and excise station]_

at **(..SPECIFY THE PLACE OF REMOVAL..), with intent to evade the

(K)_[prohibition]_
(L)_[restriction]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 50(2)(b), (4) and (5) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

Submit a form Crimsec 38 where drugs are seized

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.
